name: Kachhi / Kachi Koli Gujarati
confidence_why: Known only second-hand, as quoted in another work.

catalog_quote: The author also very briefly presented some phonological features such as syllable types, length, stress and palatalization. ... Vowel length[24] is phonemic and the long vowels receive greater stress, as shown in the following examples (lighter stress is marked with a single superscript bar (ˈ) and the heavier stress is marked with two bars (ˈˈ)): /ˈman/ ‘heart’ /ˈˈmaan/ ‘with difficulty’ According to the author, stress in Kachhi falls on the penultimate syllable of the word. Examples are as follows: /taˈˈmaaroo/ ‘your’ /bbaˈˈtriizoo/ ‘nephew’ /ˈparaa/ ‘over there’ /ˈbbilaph/ ‘light bulb’ However, if the vowel in final syllable is long, followed by a consonant, the final syllable will receive greater stress. For example: /ˈpara/ ‘over there’ /paˈˈraaR/ ‘chaff’

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word stress on the penultimate syllable; a final syllable containing a long vowel closed by a consonant (superheavy CVVC) takes the stress instead (final open long vowel, e.g. /ˈparaa/, and final closed short vowel, e.g. /ˈbbilaph/, do not attract it). Long vowels are described as carrying heavier stress than short vowels.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described as such; Woodland (per Zubair) distinguishes 'lighter' (ˈ) vs 'heavier' (ˈˈ) stress, the heavier degree going to long vowels.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress when the final syllable has a long vowel followed by a consonant (/paˈˈraaR/ 'chaff').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, isolated citation forms from a brief unpublished phonology sketch; 'the author' = Woodland (1991). Zubair's 'Kachhi' = Kachi Koli [gjk] (his fn. 8 and Figure: 'W. Gujarati: Kachhi Koli'), not Kachchhi/Kutchi [kfr].
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted passage is Zubair's (2016) summary of Woodland's unpublished 1991 'Phonology sketch of Kachi Koli Gujarati'; Zubair spells the language 'Kachhi' but identifies it as Kachi/Kachhi Koli [gjk] of the Gujarati group (kach1272), not Kachchhi/Kutchi [kfr, kach1277]. Zubair's own first-hand analysis in the same thesis (penultimate stress, final if the final syllable is heavy; sec. 4.6 pp. 89-93) is for WADIYARI = Wadiyara Koli [kxp, wadi1248], a separate Glottolog language with 78% lexical similarity to Kachi Koli, and must not be entered under kach1272.

sources.note: Second-hand for Kachi Koli (p. 34, reporting Woodland 1991 ms): long vowels receive greater stress; stress falls on the penultimate syllable; but if the final syllable has a long vowel followed by a consonant, the final syllable receives greater stress (/taˈˈmaaroo/ 'your' vs /paˈˈraaR/ 'chaff'). First-hand for Wadiyari (different language): predictable, penultimate, final if final syllable heavy (abstract iii-iv; sec. 4.6 pp. 89-93).
